instruction: I'm tracking which Hong Kong restaurants I've visited from my list. Could you please add a new column titled 'Visited' in column E of the spreadsheet? Then, for each of the 5 restaurants (rows 2-6), please fill in either YES or NO to indicate whether I've visited them. You can choose any combination of YES/NO values for the restaurants. Make sure to save the file when you're done.

metadata.explanation: Task requires adding a 'Visited' column header in E1 and filling E2:E6 with YES/NO values. Evaluator checks: (1) E1 contains 'Visited' header (50% score), (2) At least 3 cells in E2:E6 contain valid YES/NO values (50% score). This allows partial credit for completing parts of the task.
metadata.scoring_breakdown: 0.5 for correct header, 0.5 for at least 3 valid YES/NO values

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator correctly extracts column E data (header from E1, values from E2:E6)
Metric function correctly handles expected parameter as rules dict (expected.get('header'), expected.get('valid_values'))
Postconfig appropriately saves the file before verification
Complete coverage: both header and YES/NO values are verified
Minor issue: Metric requires only 3/5 cells to have valid values, but instruction implies all 5 restaurants should be filled. This makes verification more lenient than instruction requires.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Consider changing line 42 in metrics/xlsx.py from 'if non_empty_count >= 3 and valid_count >= 3' to 'if non_empty_count >= 5 and valid_count >= 5' to ensure all 5 restaurant rows are filled as instruction implies

The static warning about 'second parameter type (Any) may not match expected.rules type (Dict)' is a false positive - the metric correctly accesses expected as a dict since type='rule' means expected IS the rules dict
